actions-list.actionItem: The House has concluded all anticipated legislative business and has proceeded to Special Order speeches.
The House proceeded with further one minute speeches.
The House observed a moment of silence in remembrance of the victims of the recent tragedy at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon.
Mr. Griffith asked unanimous consent that when the House adjourns today, it adjourn to meet at 11:00 a.m. on November 11. Agreed to without objection.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.

actions-list.header: On agreeing to the resolution Agreed to by recorded vote: 215
On ordering the previous question Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: 213

actions-list.actionItem: Considered as unfinished business. H. Res. 1650 — "Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1013) to amend the Federal securities laws to enhance 403(b) plans, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.

actions-list.header: On motion to refer Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: 211

actions-list.actionItem: The previous question on the motion to refer was ordered without objection.
The House proceeded with one hour of debate on motion to refer H. Res. 1655.
Mr. Issa moved to refer to the Judiciary.
Considered as privileged matter. H. Res. 1655 — "Impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, for high crimes and misdemeanors."

actions-list.header: QUESTION OF THE PRIVILEGES OF THE HOUSE
actions-list.actionItem: Mr. Massie rose to a question of the privileges of the House and offered the resolution. The Chair directed the Clerk to report the resolution. Upon examination of the resolution, the Chair determined that the resolution did constitute a question of the privileges of the House.
The House convened, returning from a recess continuing the legislative day of November 10.
The Speaker announced that the House do now recess. The next meeting is subject to the call of the Chair.

At the conclusion of debate on H. Res. 1650, the Chair put the question on ordering the previous question and by voice vote, announced that the ayes had prevailed. Mr. McGovern demanded the yeas and nays and the Chair postponed further proceedings until a time to be announced.
The House proceeded with one hour of debate on H. Res. 1650.
Considered as privileged matter. H. Res. 1650 — "Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1013) to amend the Federal securities laws to enhance 403(b) plans, and for other purposes."
The House proceeded with one minute speeches which by direction of the Chair, would be limited to 15 per side of the aisle.
The Chair designated Mr. McGovern to lead the Members in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.
The Speaker announced approval of the Journal.  Pursuant to clause 1, rule I, the Journal stands approved.
Today's prayer was offered by the House Chaplain, Chaplain Margaret Grun Kibben.
The House convened, returning from a recess continuing the legislative day of November 10.
The Speaker announced that the House do now recess. The next meeting is scheduled for 12:00 P.M. today.
The House proceeded with Morning-Hour Debate. At the conclusion of Morning-Hour, the House will recess until 12:00 p.m. for the start of legislative business.
The Speaker designated the Honorable Earl L. "Buddy" Carter to act as Speaker pro tempore for today.
The House convened, starting a new legislative day.
